facts.raw_span: Visual acuity: 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes (OU)
Few yellow spots present, no pigmentary degeneration
Indistinct grayish circle beyond the arcades
Large, slow scotopic and photopic responses
Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in superotemporal region

concepts.why: The patient's night blindness since childhood, flat rod electroretinogram, and complete loss of photoreceptors in the superotemporal region are consistent with Retinitis pigmentosa.
The patient's night blindness, flat rod electroretinogram, and superotemporal zones showing hypofluorescence are consistent with Choroideremia.
The patient's night blindness, flat rod electroretinogram, and complete loss of photoreceptors in the superotemporal region are consistent with Gyrate atrophy.
The patient's night blindness since childhood, normal color vision, and flat rod electroretinogram are consistent with Congenital stationary night blindness.
The patient's night blindness, flat rod electroretinogram, and complete loss of photoreceptors in the superotemporal region are consistent with Leber congenital amaurosis.
The patient's Goldmann visual field showing an inferonasal scotoma is consistent with choroidal dystrophy, which can cause progressive visual field loss.

rationales.F01: Night blindness since childhood is a key symptom of retinal disorders
rationales.F09: Flat rod electroretinogram is a characteristic finding in retinitis pigmentosa and other retinal disorders
rationales.F11: Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium is a characteristic finding in advanced retinal disorders

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's night blindness since childhood, flat rod electroretinogram, and complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in the superotemporal region support Retinitis pigmentosa, with Choroideremia as a close runner-up due to similar findings, but Retinitis pigmentosa better explains the overall clinical presentation.
